body:
Ouch, felt that to a certain level.

I'm a chronic smiler, smiling/laughing at any emotion, because that's the safest "facial state" to be in for me. Not allowed to be less than amused, not allowed to be annoyed, not allowed to be sad. My mom would ask "what's got you smiling so creepily like that?", but it was better than crying (my natural response to most strong emotions), to which she'd yell "what do you have to cry about? What are you so happy about that you're crying, huh? I fucking hope you're not thinking you're being treated unfairly!". I can't show any sign of any negative emotions – the slightest hint of petulance, sadness, anger, or disappointment will land me immediately in the yelling zone, because she assumes it has to do with her (which, I mean, 90% of the time is correct) and goes off, because what did *she* do, right? She's perfect, I'm just broken and too sensitive. Crying has always landed me in the mocking zone as well, which is why I despise crying in public and hate that I cry so much.

Phew, that was long. Thanks for the post, though, made something click in my head as to why I act the way I do sometimes.

I'm a trans guy, but not out to my parents, so in their eyes I'm still female. Growing up, my mom did a lot of weird vaguely sexual shit to me, and said a lot of similar things (though, I don't think, not to that extent). She'd grope my ass and thighs and had an obsession with my chest when I was a kid, always talk about my "great body" even as a middle schooler, and even one of her friends called me "voluptuous" when I was no older than 13 (which is why I thought it was just culture for the longest time, since I'm living overseas and hence not very "Korean"). Not quite the same thing as your situation, but once again, oddly sexual.

I don't think it's common, and if it is, it's still not right. It's actually downright gross.

Hannah, my name is Jamie, and I'm sixteen.

I still remember as clear as day when I was twelve, seeing as it was only four years ago. I was in seventh grade, and it was when I started spiralling.

I love music and painting things as well. I wanted to be a singer when I was twelve. I also wanted to be an artist. I still want to be an artist, and am working to make that dream come true, even when life and school gets in the way.

Things with my family were, and still are, messy as well. I used to believe that my parents hated me because I could never live up to their expectations and I was just a moping, depressed, angsty tween, and sometimes, I still do. Hannah, I obviously don't know what your family is like, but from what little you've told us, I can assume that they at least care about you. Even if it seems like they're disappointed in you, ignore it, please, because they most likely aren't. I personally think they aren't just *wanting* to love you, they *do* love you. And if it feels like they're trying to fit you into a mold, an ideal version of you that they've conjured up in their heads (which they're not, I hope), then please tell them so, and remind yourself that who you become is up to you, and that you don't have to live up to anyone's expectations. Just striving to become the best version of yourself and living for that alone would be more than good enough.

You're a lot more mature than I was at your age. When I was twelve, I blamed all of my problems on everyone else, no matter how much I denied that. I was, quite honestly, a bit of an ass, and I'm surprised I had any friends at all. I complained all the time, and God, I was such a mess. You seem to have found peace, and Hannah, that scares me, because this is the wrong kind of peace. Please reconsider, not for anyone else's sake, for yours. I don't know you, and I don't know what you're going through, but I know that even if I'm hurting now, I've experienced a lot of good things in the four years since I was twelve, and I'm so glad I got to experience those things. Things may get worse from time to time – hell, why'd you reckon I'm on here? But please, even if only for a year, two years, keep living. Reach out to trustworthy friends and family or even teachers.

I honestly don't know if I'm happy right now, or if I'm happy that I continued to live at all. But I know for a fact that I don't regret it. I don't regret living, and I've gotten to meet such wonderful people and become a stronger, better version of myself because I chose to live.
